claims.text: As-cast, Co-free FeNiCrMn contains inherent microstructural heterogeneities.
The dynamic mechanical behavior of as-cast FeNiCrMn is governed by competition between thermally activated dislocation glide and localized adiabatic shear-band formation.
High strain rate increases the yield strength of FeNiCrMn.
Low temperature limits thermal activation and hinders dislocation motion in FeNiCrMn.
High strain rate produces dislocation drag in FeNiCrMn.
Hindered dislocation motion promotes dislocation pile-ups in FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation pile-ups trigger localized adiabatic shear bands in FeNiCrMn.
Adiabatic shear bands concentrate plastic deformation.
Adiabatic shear-band formation enhances yield strength in FeNiCrMn.
Adiabatic shear-band formation reduces ductility in FeNiCrMn.
High-strain-rate, low-temperature deformation of FeNiCrMn produces elevated local dislocation densities and visible adiabatic shear bands.
Elevated temperature increases dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery in FeNiCrMn.
Increased dislocation mobility and recovery suppress shear-band formation and make deformation more homogeneous.
Higher-temperature FeNiCrMn has lower yield strength and improved ductility.
Under quasi-static room-temperature loading, FeNiCrMn deforms relatively homogeneously and has lower yield strength and higher ductility than under high-rate, low-temperature loading.
Post-solidification processing or annealing can alter the cast microstructure and move the material outside the proposed hypothesis boundary.
The strain-rate and temperature thresholds for shear-band-dominated deformation may vary with composition and microstructure.
A controlled matrix spanning approximately 77–500 K and 10^-3–10^3 s^-1, with stress-strain, imaging, temperature-mapping, SEM, and TEM measurements, can test the proposed correlations.
Failure to observe the predicted strength-ductility trend or localized adiabatic shear bands under high-rate, low-temperature loading would falsify the hypothesis.
